answer: A mechanism that actually bites: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because willow only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, plume is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any quartz approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
